title: My apartment has four doors. Tonight I counted five, and someone's snoring behind the new one.
story:
Someone was snoring behind a door that wasn't there yesterday.

It was in my hallway, between the bathroom and the closet. Plain white, brass knob. My apartment has four doors, and I live alone. I always leave the hallway light on at night. The dark has scared me since I was a kid.

I pressed my ear to the wood. Slow breathing. A small dry cough. My cough.

So I opened it.

Behind it was my hallway again. Same rug, same coats, but dark. At the end, my bedroom door hung open, and someone was asleep in my bed, facing the wall, wearing my gray shirt.

I stepped through to see his face. The snoring stopped. I ran back, slammed the door, and sat on the couch with every lamp on, staring at it until sunrise.

At six, my bedroom door opened behind me. I didn't turn around. Calm footsteps walked past, through the new door. The lock clicked. Then the door was just wall.

I laughed. I got up to switch off the hallway light.

It was already off.

This was never my hallway.
premise: a fifth door in the hallway opens onto a dark copy of the narrator's apartment with his double asleep; at dawn the double walks back through and the door vanishes; the hallway light he always leaves on is off, so he's on the wrong side
